42/// @brief Formats a flag.
43/// @param value The flag.
44/// @return `true` or `false`.
45[[nodiscard]] inline std::string formatBool(bool value) { return value ? "true" : "false"; }

47/// @brief Escapes text with a backslash: a line break becomes backslash and `n`, a carriage return backslash and `r`,
48/// and a backslash or a character @p isSpecial selects is preceded by a backslash.
49/// @tparam Special A callable taking a `char` and returning whether to escape it.
50/// @param text The text.
51/// @param isSpecial Selects the characters to escape besides the backslash and the two line-ending characters.
52/// @return The escaped text.
53template <typename Special>
54[[nodiscard]] std::string escape(std::string_view text, Special const& isSpecial) {
55 std::string escaped;
56 escaped.reserve(text.size());
57 for (char const character : text) {
58 if (character == '\n') {
59 escaped += "\\n";
60 } else if (character == '\r') {
61 escaped += "\\r";
62 } else {
63 if (character == '\\' || isSpecial(character)) {
64 escaped += '\\';
65 }
66 escaped += character;
67 }
68 }
69 return escaped;
70}
71
72/// @brief Formats free text as a property value. Line breaks and `=` are escaped, so the value stays on its own line
73/// and no part of it reads as another `name=value`.
74/// @param text The text, UTF-8.
75/// @return The escaped text.
76[[nodiscard]] inline std::string formatText(std::string_view text) {
77 return escape(text, [](char character) { return character == '='; });
78}
79
80/// @brief Formats free text as an element of a `formatList` list. Also escapes `,`, `[` and `]`, so the text reads as
81/// one element.
82/// @param text The text, UTF-8.
83/// @return The escaped text.
84[[nodiscard]] inline std::string formatItem(std::string_view text) {
85 return escape(text, [](char character) { return std::string_view{"=,[]"}.contains(character); });
86}

88/// @brief Formats a menu's entries: `[a,b]`, each entry its label followed by the attributes that differ from the
89/// default, as `;icon=x`, `;keys=x`, `;checked=true` or `;checked=false`, and `;enabled=false`, then its
90/// submenu in brackets. A flat menu of plain entries reads `[Open,Quit]`.
91/// @param entries The entries.
92/// @return Their text; `=`, `,`, `[`, `]` and `;` in a label or attribute are escaped.
93// NOLINTNEXTLINE(misc-no-recursion): a submenu is formatted as a menu one level down.
94[[nodiscard]] inline std::string formatMenu(std::vector<MenuEntry> const& entries) {
95 auto const text = [](std::string_view value) {
96 return escape(value, [](char character) { return std::string_view{"=,[];"}.contains(character); });
97 };
98 std::string formatted = "[";
99 for (MenuEntry const& entry : entries) {
100 formatted += formatted.size() == 1 ? "" : ",";
101 if (entry.separator) {
102 formatted += ";separator";
103 continue;
104 }
105 formatted += text(entry.label);
106 if (!entry.icon.empty()) {
107 formatted += ";icon=" + text(entry.icon);
108 }
109 if (!entry.keys.empty()) {
110 formatted += ";keys=" + text(entry.keys);
111 }
112 if (entry.checked.has_value()) {
113 formatted += std::string{";checked="} + (*entry.checked ? "true" : "false");
114 }
115 if (!entry.enabled) {
116 formatted += ";enabled=false";
117 }
118 if (!entry.description.empty()) {
119 formatted += ";description=" + text(entry.description);
120 }
121 if (!entry.items.empty()) {
122 formatted += formatMenu(entry.items);
123 }
124 }
125 return formatted + "]";
126}

128/// @brief Formats a key: an integer in decimal, a string in double quotes, so `7` and `"7"` differ.
129/// @param key The key.
130/// @return Its text. A string key is escaped as `formatItem` escapes, and a double quote in it is preceded by a
131/// backslash.
132[[nodiscard]] inline std::string formatKey(Key const& key) {
133 if (auto const* const number = std::get_if<std::int64_t>(&key); number != nullptr) {
134 return std::to_string(*number);
135 }
136 return '"' +
137 escape(std::get<std::string>(key),
138 [](char character) { return std::string_view{"=,[]\""}.contains(character); }) +
139 '"';
140}
141
142/// @brief Formats an optional key.

145[[nodiscard]] inline std::string formatOptionalKey(std::optional<Key> const& key) {
146 return key.has_value() ? formatKey(*key) : std::string{"none"};
147}

201/// @brief Formats a size request.
202/// @param hints The request.
203/// @return `width/height`, each as `formatSizing` gives it and followed by ` min=<n>` and ` max=<n>` for the bounds
204/// it has, then ` self=<align>` when the node places itself, such as `stretch(1) max=44/content self=center`.
205[[nodiscard]] inline std::string formatLayout(LayoutHints const& hints) {
206 auto const bounds = [](std::optional<int> minimum, std::optional<int> maximum) {
207 std::string text;
208 if (minimum) {
209 text += " min=" + std::to_string(*minimum);
210 }
211 if (maximum) {
212 text += " max=" + std::to_string(*maximum);
213 }
214 return text;
215 };
216 return formatSizing(hints.width) + bounds(hints.minWidth, hints.maxWidth) + "/" + formatSizing(hints.height) +
217 bounds(hints.minHeight, hints.maxHeight) +
218 (hints.alignSelf ? " self=" + formatAlign(*hints.alignSelf) : std::string{}) +
219 (hints.bleed ? " bleed" : std::string{});
220}

222/// @brief Formats a date-time value.
223/// @param value The value.
224/// @return `none` for `nullopt`, `empty` for an empty `Timestamp`, else the ISO-8601 UTC instant.
225[[nodiscard]] inline std::string formatTimestamp(std::optional<morph::time::Timestamp> const& value) {
226 if (!value.has_value()) {
227 return "none";
228 }
229 if (!value->hasValue()) {
230 return "empty";
231 }
232 return (**value).toIso8601();
233}

235/// @brief Formats a list as `[a,b,c]`.
236/// @tparam T The element type.
237/// @tparam F A callable turning a `T const&` into a `std::string`.
238/// @param items The elements.
239/// @param each Formats one element.
240/// @return The list's text.
241template <typename T, typename F>
242[[nodiscard]] std::string formatList(std::vector<T> const& items, F const& each) {
243 std::string text = "[";
244 bool first = true;
245 for (T const& item : items) {
246 if (!first) {
247 text += ',';
248 }
249 first = false;
250 text += each(item);
251 }
252 return text + "]";
253}

392/// @brief Formats runs of text: `[Lot ,L-26-0381;mono,7;tone=Err]`, each run its text followed by `;strong`, `;mono`
393/// and `;tone=<tone>` when set.
394/// @param spans The runs.
395/// @return Their text; `=`, `,`, `[`, `]` and `;` in a run are escaped, so a run cannot forge a flag.
396[[nodiscard]] inline std::string formatSpans(std::vector<TextSpan> const& spans) {
397 std::string formatted = "[";
398 for (TextSpan const& span : spans) {
399 formatted += formatted.size() == 1 ? "" : ",";
400 formatted += escape(span.text, [](char character) { return std::string_view{"=,[];"}.contains(character); });
401 formatted += span.strong ? ";strong" : "";
402 formatted += span.mono ? ";mono" : "";
403 formatted += span.action ? ";action" : "";
404 if (span.tone != Tone::Neutral) {
405 formatted += ";tone=";
406 formatted += enumName(span.tone);
407 }
408 }
409 return formatted + "]";
410}
411
412/// @brief The characters of runs as `formatSpans` records them: each run's text up to its first unescaped `;`, joined.
413/// @param recorded The recorded runs, `[a,b;strong]`; anything shorter than the brackets reads as no characters.
414/// @return Their text, unescaped.
415[[nodiscard]] inline std::string spansCharacters(std::string_view recorded) {
416 std::string joined;
417 if (recorded.size() < 2) {
418 return joined;
419 }
420 std::string_view const inner = recorded.substr(1, recorded.size() - 2);
421 bool flags = false;
422 for (std::size_t at = 0; at < inner.size(); ++at) {
423 char const character = inner.at(at);
424 if (character == '\\' && at + 1 < inner.size()) {
425 ++at;
426 if (!flags) {
427 joined += inner.at(at) == 'n' ? '\n' : inner.at(at);
428 }
429 } else if (character == ',') {
430 flags = false;
431 } else if (character == ';') {
432 flags = true;
433 } else if (!flags) {
434 joined += character;
435 }
436 }
437 return joined;
438}

540/// @brief The handlers a widget was given, which the interaction helpers call.

594/// @brief One fake widget's state.
595struct Record {
596 /// @brief The widget's id: its creation number, from 1.
597 int id = 0;
598 /// @brief The kind shown in the log and the dump.
599 std::string kind;
600 /// @brief The parent's id; 0 for a root.
601 int parent = 0;
602 /// @brief The children's ids, in order.
603 std::vector<int> children;
604 /// @brief Every property set so far, formatted, in name order.
605 std::map<std::string, std::string, std::less<>> props;
606 /// @brief The handlers set so far.
607 Callbacks callbacks;
608 /// @brief The drag key, as `setDragKey` last set it.
609 std::optional<Key> dragKey;
610 /// @brief The chords, as `setKeys` last set them.
611 std::vector<std::string> chords;
612 /// @brief A menu's entries, as `setItems` last set them.
613 std::vector<MenuEntry> menu;
614 /// @brief The fake widget object.
615 Widget* widget = nullptr;
616 /// @brief Called with a child's id once that child is destroyed; a fake table re-marks its selection with it.
617 std::function<void(int)> onChildDestroyed;
618};

620/// @brief The records, the roots and the operation log that every fake widget of one backend writes to.
621///
622/// Held by `shared_ptr` from the backend and from every fake, so a fake that outlives its backend still has
623/// somewhere to record its destruction.
624class RecordStore {
625public:
626 /// @brief Records a new widget appended to @p parent and logs its creation.
627 /// @param kind The kind shown in the log and the dump.
628 /// @param parent The container it is appended to, or null for a root.
629 /// @param widget The fake widget.
630 /// @param initial Properties fixed at creation; recorded without a log line.
631 /// @return The new widget's id.
632 int create(std::string kind, Widget const* parent, Widget& widget, PropList initial) {
633 int const widgetId = ++_nextId;
634 int const parentId = parent == nullptr ? 0 : idOf(*parent);
635 Record record{.id = widgetId, .kind = std::move(kind), .parent = parentId, .widget = &widget};
636 for (auto& [name, value] : initial) {
637 record.props.insert_or_assign(std::move(name), std::move(value));
638 }
639 _log.push_back("create " + label(record) + " in " +
640 (parentId == 0 ? std::string{"root"} : label(at(parentId))));
641 siblingsOf(parentId).push_back(widgetId);
642 _ids.insert_or_assign(&widget, widgetId);
643 _records.insert_or_assign(widgetId, std::move(record));
644 return widgetId;
645 }
646
647 /// @brief Sets a property through a widget setter, and logs it.
648 /// @param widgetId The widget.
649 /// @param name The property.
650 /// @param value Its formatted value.
651 void set(int widgetId, std::string_view name, std::string value) {
652 Record& record = at(widgetId);
653 _log.push_back("set " + label(record) + " " + std::string{name} + "=" + value);
654 record.props.insert_or_assign(std::string{name}, std::move(value));
655 }
656
657 /// @brief Sets a property the user changed through the widget itself; no setter ran, so nothing is logged.
658 /// @param widgetId The widget.
659 /// @param name The property.
660 /// @param value Its formatted value.
661 void setByUser(int widgetId, std::string_view name, std::string value) {
662 at(widgetId).props.insert_or_assign(std::string{name}, std::move(value));
663 }
664
665 /// @brief Moves a widget among its siblings, as `ContainerWidget::moveChild` defines it, and logs it.
666 /// @param widgetId The widget.
667 /// @param index The new position; past the end means last.
668 // An id and a position: an `int` and a `std::size_t`, which convert into each other.
669 // NOLINTNEXTLINE(bugprone-easily-swappable-parameters)
670 void move(int widgetId, std::size_t index) {
671 Record const& record = at(widgetId);
672 std::vector<int>& siblings = siblingsOf(record.parent);
673 std::erase(siblings, widgetId);
674 auto const position = static_cast<std::ptrdiff_t>(std::min(index, siblings.size()));
675 siblings.insert(siblings.begin() + position, widgetId);
676 _log.push_back("move " + label(record) + " to " + std::to_string(index));
677 }
678
679 /// @brief Forgets a destroyed widget and logs it. Its remaining children become roots.
680 /// @param widgetId The widget; an unknown id does nothing.
681 void destroy(int widgetId) {
682 auto const found = _records.find(widgetId);
683 if (found == _records.end()) {
684 return;
685 }
686 Record const& record = found->second;
687 int const parentId = record.parent;
688 _log.push_back("destroy " + label(record));
689 std::erase(siblingsOf(parentId), widgetId);
690 for (int const child : record.children) {
691 if (auto const orphan = _records.find(child); orphan != _records.end()) {
692 orphan->second.parent = 0;
693 _roots.push_back(child);
694 }
695 }
696 if (_focused == widgetId) {
697 _focused = 0;
698 }
699 _ids.erase(record.widget);
700 _records.erase(found);
701 if (auto const parent = _records.find(parentId); parent != _records.end()) {
702 if (auto const notify = parent->second.onChildDestroyed; notify) {
703 notify(widgetId);
704 }
705 }
706 }
707
708 /// @brief A widget's record.
709 /// @param widgetId The widget.
710 /// @return The record.
711 /// @throws std::out_of_range for an id that names no live widget.
712 [[nodiscard]] Record& at(int widgetId) {
713 auto const found = _records.find(widgetId);
714 if (found == _records.end()) {
715 throw std::out_of_range{"RecordingBackend: no widget #" + std::to_string(widgetId)};
716 }
717 return found->second;
718 }
719
720 /// @brief A widget's record.
721 /// @param widgetId The widget.
722 /// @return The record.
723 /// @throws std::out_of_range for an id that names no live widget.
724 [[nodiscard]] Record const& at(int widgetId) const {
725 auto const found = _records.find(widgetId);
726 if (found == _records.end()) {
727 throw std::out_of_range{"RecordingBackend: no widget #" + std::to_string(widgetId)};
728 }
729 return found->second;
730 }
731
732 /// @brief The id of a live widget made by this store's backend.
733 /// @param widget The widget.
734 /// @return Its id.
735 /// @throws std::out_of_range when @p widget is not one of them.
736 [[nodiscard]] int idOf(Widget const& widget) const {
737 auto const found = _ids.find(&widget);
738 if (found == _ids.end()) {
739 throw std::out_of_range{"RecordingBackend: not a live widget of this backend"};
740 }
741 return found->second;
742 }
743
744 /// @brief Every live widget's record.
745 /// @return The records, by id.
746 [[nodiscard]] std::map<int, Record> const& records() const noexcept { return _records; }
747
748 /// @brief The operation log.
749 /// @return One line per operation, oldest first.
750 [[nodiscard]] std::vector<std::string> const& log() const noexcept { return _log; }
751
752 /// @brief Empties the operation log.
753 void clearLog() noexcept { _log.clear(); }
754
755 /// @brief Records that keyboard focus moved to a widget, and logs `focus`.
756 /// @param widgetId The widget that took focus.
757 /// @throws std::out_of_range for an id that names no live widget.
758 void focus(int widgetId) {
759 _log.push_back("focus " + label(at(widgetId)));
760 _focused = widgetId;
761 }
762
763 /// @brief The widget that last took focus.
764 /// @return Its id, or 0 when none has, or it has since been destroyed.
765 [[nodiscard]] int focused() const noexcept { return _focused; }
766
767 /// @brief The golden tree.
768 /// @return One line per live widget, children indented two spaces per depth.
769 [[nodiscard]] std::string dump() const {
770 std::string text;
771 for (int const root : _roots) {
772 dumpInto(text, root, 0);
773 }
774 return text;
775 }
776
777private:
778 [[nodiscard]] static std::string label(Record const& record) {
779 return record.kind + "#" + std::to_string(record.id);
780 }
781
782 std::vector<int>& siblingsOf(int parentId) { return parentId == 0 ? _roots : at(parentId).children; }
783
784 // A widget tree is dumped by descending it. The id and the depth are an `int` and a `std::size_t`, which convert
785 // into each other.
786 // NOLINTNEXTLINE(misc-no-recursion,bugprone-easily-swappable-parameters)
787 void dumpInto(std::string& text, int widgetId, std::size_t depth) const {
788 Record const& record = at(widgetId);
789 text.append(depth * 2, ' ');
790 text += label(record);
791 for (auto const& [name, value] : record.props) {
792 text += ' ';
793 text += name;
794 text += '=';
795 text += value;
796 }
797 text += '\n';
798 for (int const child : record.children) {
799 dumpInto(text, child, depth + 1);
800 }
801 }
802
803 std::map<int, Record> _records;
804 std::unordered_map<Widget const*, int> _ids;
805 std::vector<int> _roots;
806 std::vector<std::string> _log;
807 int _nextId = 0;
808 int _focused = 0;
809};
810
811/// @brief The `Widget` half of every fake: records itself on construction, records `Common`'s setters, and records
812/// its destruction.
813/// @tparam Interface The widget interface the fake implements.
814template <typename Interface>
815class FakeLeaf : public Interface {
816public:
817 /// @brief Records the new widget, appended to @p parent, and logs its creation.
818 /// @param store Where the widget records itself.
819 /// @param kind The kind shown in the log and the dump.
820 /// @param parent The container it is appended to (or the button whose content it is), or null for a root.
821 /// @param initial Properties fixed at creation.
822 FakeLeaf(std::shared_ptr<RecordStore> store, std::string kind, Widget const* parent, PropList initial = {})
823 : _store{std::move(store)}, _id{_store->create(std::move(kind), parent, *this, std::move(initial))} {}
824
825 /// @brief Forgets the widget and logs its destruction; its remaining children become roots.
826 ~FakeLeaf() override {
827 try {
828 _store->destroy(_id);
829 } catch (...) { // NOLINT(bugprone-empty-catch)
830 // Logging the destruction failed to allocate; the record stays, and a test reads it as a leak.
831 }
832 }
833
834 FakeLeaf(FakeLeaf const&) = delete;
835 FakeLeaf& operator=(FakeLeaf const&) = delete;
836 FakeLeaf(FakeLeaf&&) = delete;
837 FakeLeaf& operator=(FakeLeaf&&) = delete;
838
839 /// @brief Records property `visible`.
840 /// @param visible Whether it is shown.
841 void setVisible(bool visible) override { set("visible", formatBool(visible)); }
842
843 /// @brief Records property `enabled`.
844 /// @param enabled Whether it accepts input.
845 void setEnabled(bool enabled) override { set("enabled", formatBool(enabled)); }
846
847 /// @brief Records property `layout`, as `formatLayout` gives it.
848 /// @param hints The request in both dimensions.
849 void setLayout(LayoutHints const& hints) override { set("layout", formatLayout(hints)); }
850
851 /// @brief Records property `dragKey` and keeps the key for `RecordingBackend::drag`.
852 /// @param key Engaged: the key a drop delivers. `nullopt`: not draggable.
853 void setDragKey(std::optional<Key> const& key) override {
854 _store->at(_id).dragKey = key;
855 set("dragKey", formatOptionalKey(key));
856 }
857
858 /// @brief Records property `drop=handler` and keeps both handlers for `RecordingBackend::drag`.
859 /// @param accepts Whether a dragged key may be dropped here.
860 /// @param onDrop Called with the key on a drop that `accepts` allowed.
861 void setDropHandler(std::function<bool(Key const&)> accepts, std::function<void(Key)> onDrop) override {
862 Callbacks& handlers = callbacks();
863 handlers.accepts = std::move(accepts);
864 handlers.drop = std::move(onDrop);
865 set("drop", "handler");
866 }
867
868 /// @brief Records property `a11yName`.
869 /// @param name The accessible name.
870 void setAccessibleName(std::string_view name) override { set("a11yName", formatText(name)); }
871
872 /// @brief Records property `a11yRole`.
873 /// @param role The role.
874 void setAccessibleRole(std::string_view role) override { set("a11yRole", formatText(role)); }
875
876 /// @brief Records property `testId`.
877 /// @param testId The identifier.
878 void setTestId(std::string_view testId) override { set("testId", formatText(testId)); }
879
880 /// @brief Records property `tooltip`.
881 /// @param text The tooltip.
882 void setTooltip(std::string_view text) override { set("tooltip", formatText(text)); }
883
884 /// @brief Records property `surface`.
885 /// @param surface The surface's name.
886 void setSurface(std::string_view surface) override { set("surface", formatText(surface)); }
887
888 /// @brief Records property `keys`, the chords joined by commas, and keeps the chords and the handler for
889 /// `RecordingBackend::press`.
890 /// @param chords The chords.
891 /// @param onChord Called with the chord that was pressed.
892 void setKeys(std::vector<std::string> const& chords, std::function<void(std::string)> onChord) override {
893 Record& record = _store->at(_id);
894 record.callbacks.chord = std::move(onChord);
895 record.chords = chords;
896 std::string joined;
897 for (std::string const& chord : chords) {
898 joined += joined.empty() ? "" : ",";
899 joined += chord;
900 }
901 set("keys", formatText(joined));
902 }
903
904 /// @brief Moves the backend's recorded focus here, and logs `focus`.
905 void focus() override { _store->focus(_id); }
906
907 /// @brief Keeps the handler for `RecordingBackend::hover`.
908 /// @param onHover The handler.
909 void setOnHover(std::function<void()> onHover) override { _store->at(_id).callbacks.hover = std::move(onHover); }
910
911protected:
912 /// @brief Records a property set through a setter.
913 /// @param name The property.
914 /// @param value Its formatted value.
915 void set(std::string_view name, std::string value) { _store->set(_id, name, std::move(value)); }
916
917 /// @brief This widget's handlers.
918 /// @return The handlers, for a setter to store into.
919 [[nodiscard]] Callbacks& callbacks() { return _store->at(_id).callbacks; }
920
921 /// @brief The store this widget records into.
922 /// @return The store.
923 [[nodiscard]] RecordStore& store() const noexcept { return *_store; }
924
925 /// @brief The store, shared: what a part this widget makes (an overlay's footer) records into.
926 /// @return The store.
927 [[nodiscard]] std::shared_ptr<RecordStore> const& sharedStore() const noexcept { return _store; }
928
929 /// @brief This widget's id.
930 /// @return The id.
931 [[nodiscard]] int id() const noexcept { return _id; }
932
933private:
934 std::shared_ptr<RecordStore> _store;
935 int _id;
936};

938/// @brief The `ContainerWidget` half of every fake container.
939/// @tparam Interface The container interface the fake implements.
940template <typename Interface>
941class FakeContainer : public FakeLeaf<Interface> {
942public:
943 using FakeLeaf<Interface>::FakeLeaf;
944
945 /// @brief Moves a child among its siblings and logs it.
946 /// @param child One of this container's children.
947 /// @param index The new position; past the end means last.
948 /// @throws std::logic_error when @p child is not this container's child.
949 void moveChild(Widget& child, std::size_t index) override {
950 RecordStore& records = this->store();
951 int const childId = records.idOf(child);
952 if (records.at(childId).parent != this->id()) {
953 throw std::logic_error{"RecordingBackend: moveChild of a widget that is not this container's child"};
954 }
955 records.move(childId, index);
956 }
957};

1066/// @brief A fake `TextInputWidget`: properties `mode`, `text`, `placeholder`, `unit`, `prefix`, `decimals`, `icon`,
1067/// `emphasis`, `mono`, `align`,
1068/// `caption`, `captionShown`, the field state, and a text cursor.
1069///
1070/// The cursor is a byte offset into the text. A user's edit puts it where the edit left it; `setText` with the text
1071/// the field shows leaves it alone, as the contract requires, and `setText` with another text puts it at the end.
1072class FakeTextInput final : public FakeField<TextInputWidget> {
1073public:
1074 using FakeField<TextInputWidget>::FakeField;
1075
1076 /// @brief Records property `text`; moves the cursor to the end only when the text changes.
1077 /// @param text The text, UTF-8.
1078 void setText(std::string_view text) override {
1079 if (text != _shown) {
1080 _shown = std::string{text};
1081 _cursor = _shown.size();
1082 }
1083 set("text", formatText(text));
1084 }
1085
1086 /// @brief The text the user typed: the field shows it, and the cursor is at @p cursor; nothing is logged.
1087 /// @param text The whole new text.
1088 /// @param cursor Where the cursor ends up; clamped to the text's size.
1089 void typedByUser(std::string text, std::size_t cursor) {
1090 _shown = std::move(text);
1091 _cursor = std::min(cursor, _shown.size());
1092 store().setByUser(id(), "text", formatText(_shown));
1093 }
1094
1095 /// @brief Moves the cursor as the user's arrow keys or a click would.
1096 /// @param cursor The new position; clamped to the text's size.
1097 void moveCursorByUser(std::size_t cursor) noexcept { _cursor = std::min(cursor, _shown.size()); }
1098
1099 /// @brief Where the cursor is.
1100 /// @return A byte offset into the text shown.
1101 [[nodiscard]] std::size_t cursor() const noexcept { return _cursor; }
1102
1103 /// @brief The text the field shows.
1104 /// @return The text, unformatted.
1105 [[nodiscard]] std::string const& text() const noexcept { return _shown; }
1106
1107 void setPlaceholder(std::string_view placeholder) override { set("placeholder", formatText(placeholder)); }
1108 void setUnit(std::string_view unit) override { set("unit", formatText(unit)); }
1109 void setPrefix(std::string_view prefix) override { set("prefix", formatText(prefix)); }
1110 void setMono(bool mono) override { set("mono", formatBool(mono)); }
1111 void setAlign(Align align) override {
1112 if (align == Align::End) {
1113 set("align", "end");
1114 } else {
1115 set("align", align == Align::Center ? "center" : "start");
1116 }
1117 }
1118 void setDecimals(int decimals) override { set("decimals", std::to_string(decimals)); }
1119 void setIcon(std::string_view icon) override { set("icon", formatText(icon)); }
1120 void setEmphasis(InputEmphasis emphasis) override {
1121 set("emphasis", emphasis == InputEmphasis::Prominent ? "Prominent" : "Normal");
1122 }
1123 void setCaption(std::string_view label, bool shown) override {
1124 set("caption", formatText(label));
1125 set("captionShown", formatBool(shown));
1126 }
1127 void setOnChange(std::function<void(std::string)> onChange) override { callbacks().change = std::move(onChange); }
1128 void setOnSubmit(std::function<void(std::string)> onSubmit) override { callbacks().submit = std::move(onSubmit); }
1129 void setOnCommit(std::function<void(std::string)> onCommit) override { callbacks().commit = std::move(onCommit); }
1130
1131private:
1132 std::string _shown;
1133 std::size_t _cursor = 0;
1134};

1145/// @brief A fake `SelectWidget`: properties `style`, `options`, `selected`, `caption`, `captionShown`.
1146///
1147/// `selected` shows the option the widget marks: the requested key while the options contain it, else `none`. The
1148/// requested key is kept, so options that bring it back mark it again; that re-marking is the widget's own doing and
1149/// is not logged.
1150class FakeSelect final : public FakeField<SelectWidget> {
1151public:
1152 using FakeField<SelectWidget>::FakeField;
1153
1154 /// @brief Records property `options`, and re-marks the requested key against them.
1155 /// @param options The options, in order.
1156 void setOptions(std::vector<SelectOption> const& options) override {
1157 _options = options;
1158 set("options", formatList(options, [](SelectOption const& option) {
1159 return formatKey(option.key) + ":" + formatItem(option.label);
1160 }));
1161 if (_requested.has_value()) {
1162 store().setByUser(id(), "selected", marked());
1163 }
1164 }
1165
1166 /// @brief Requests the option with @p key, and records property `selected` as the option it marks.
1167 /// @param key The key, or `nullopt` for no selection.
1168 void setSelected(std::optional<Key> const& key) override {
1169 _requested.emplace(key);
1170 set("selected", marked());
1171 }
1172
1173 /// @brief Stores the handler `RecordingBackend::choose` calls.
1174 /// @param onSelect The handler.
1175 void setOnSelect(std::function<void(Key)> onSelect) override { callbacks().select = std::move(onSelect); }
1176
1177 /// @brief Stores the handler `RecordingBackend::open` calls.
1178 /// @param onOpen The handler.
1179 void setOnOpen(Action onOpen) override { callbacks().open = std::move(onOpen); }
1180 void setCaption(std::string_view label, bool shown) override {
1181 set("caption", formatText(label));
1182 set("captionShown", formatBool(shown));
1183 }
1184
1185 /// @brief Whether one of the current options has @p key.
1186 /// @param key The key.
1187 /// @return True when an option has it.
1188 [[nodiscard]] bool offers(Key const& key) const {
1189 return std::ranges::any_of(_options, [&key](SelectOption const& option) { return option.key == key; });
1190 }
1191
1192 /// @brief Marks the option the user chose, as the requested key; nothing is logged.
1193 /// @param key The key of one of the current options.
1194 void chooseByUser(Key const& key) {
1195 _requested.emplace(key);
1196 store().setByUser(id(), "selected", marked());
1197 }
1198
1199 /// @brief The key of the option @p step places from the marked one, as Left and Right on a segmented select move.
1200 /// @param step -1 for the previous option, 1 for the next.
1201 /// @return The neighbour's key; `nullopt` when none is marked or the marked one is at that end.
1202 [[nodiscard]] std::optional<Key> neighbour(int step) const {
1203 if (!_requested.has_value() || !_requested->has_value()) {
1204 return std::nullopt;
1205 }
1206 auto const found = std::ranges::find(_options, **_requested, &SelectOption::key);
1207 if (found == _options.end()) {
1208 return std::nullopt;
1209 }
1210 auto const index = std::distance(_options.begin(), found) + step;
1211 if (index < 0 || index >= std::ssize(_options)) {
1212 return std::nullopt;
1213 }
1214 return _options.at(static_cast<std::size_t>(index)).key;
1215 }
1216
1217private:
1218 [[nodiscard]] std::string marked() const {
1219 if (!_requested.has_value() || !_requested->has_value() || !offers(**_requested)) {
1220 return "none";
1221 }
1222 return formatKey(**_requested);
1223 }
1224
1225 std::vector<SelectOption> _options;
1226 // Engaged once `setSelected` ran or the user chose; the inner value is the requested key, or none.
1227 std::optional<std::optional<Key>> _requested;
1228};
1229
1230/// @brief A fake `MenuWidget`: property `items`, and `style`, `label`, `icon` and `emphasis` of a button-style menu.
1231class FakeMenu final : public FakeLeaf<MenuWidget> {
1232public:
1233 using FakeLeaf<MenuWidget>::FakeLeaf;
1234 void setItems(std::vector<MenuEntry> const& entries) override {
1235 store().at(id()).menu = entries;
1236 set("items", formatMenu(entries));
1237 }
1238
1239 /// @brief Records properties `label`, `icon` (when given) and `emphasis` (when not `Normal`) of the trigger.
1240 /// @param trigger The trigger.
1241 void setTrigger(MenuTrigger const& trigger) override {

1524/// @brief Formats free text inside a chart property: also escapes `,`, `[`, `]`, `;`, `@` and `|`, the separators
1525/// of the chart's formats.
1526/// @param text The text, UTF-8.
1527/// @return The escaped text.
1528[[nodiscard]] inline std::string formatChartText(std::string_view text) {
1529 return escape(text, [](char character) { return std::string_view{"=,[];@|"}.contains(character); });
1530}
1531
1532/// @brief A tone's document name, as a chart's formats write it.
1533/// @param tone The tone.
1534/// @return `neutral`, `info`, `ok`, `warn` or `err`.
1535[[nodiscard]] inline std::string chartToneName(Tone tone) {
1536 static constexpr std::array<std::string_view, 5> kNames = {"neutral", "info", "ok", "warn", "err"};
1537 auto const index = static_cast<std::size_t>(tone);
1538 return index < kNames.size() ? std::string{kNames.at(index)} : std::string{"unknown"};
1539}
1540
1541/// @brief A reference line's stroke, as a chart's formats write it.
1542/// @param style The stroke.
1543/// @return `solid`, `dashed` or `dotted`.
1544[[nodiscard]] inline std::string chartStyleName(ChartLineStyle style) {
1545 if (style == ChartLineStyle::Dashed) {
1546 return "dashed";
1547 }
1548 return style == ChartLineStyle::Dotted ? "dotted" : "solid";
1549}
1550
1551/// @brief A chart point's value: the number, `gap` for none, and the number followed by `↑` or `↓` for a point
1552/// clipped at the axis's upper or lower end.
1553/// @param point The point.
1554/// @return The text.
1555[[nodiscard]] inline std::string formatChartValue(ChartPoint const& point) {
1556 if (!point.y.has_value()) {
1557 return "gap";
1558 }
1559 std::string text = std::format("{}", *point.y);
1560 if (point.clip == ChartClip::Above) {
1561 text += "↑";
1562 } else if (point.clip == ChartClip::Below) {
1563 text += "↓";
1564 }
1565 return text;
1566}
1567
1568/// @brief A chart's series: `[entry,…]`, each entry `label;joined;[point|…]` and each point
1569/// `xLabel@x,y;tone;note`, the tone empty for an unmarked point.
1570/// @param series The series.
1571/// @return The text.
1572[[nodiscard]] inline std::string formatChartSeries(std::vector<ChartSeries> const& series) {
1573 std::string text = "[";
1574 for (ChartSeries const& one : series) {
1575 text += text.size() == 1 ? "" : ",";
1576 text += formatChartText(one.label) + ";" + formatBool(one.joined) + ";[";
1577 bool first = true;
1578 for (ChartPoint const& point : one.points) {
1579 text += first ? "" : "|";
1580 first = false;
1581 text += formatChartText(point.xLabel) + "@" + std::format("{}", point.x) + "," + formatChartValue(point) +
1582 ";" + (point.tone.has_value() ? chartToneName(*point.tone) : std::string{}) + ";" +
1583 formatChartText(point.note);
1584 }
1585 text += "]";
1586 }
1587 return text + "]";
1588}
1589
1590/// @brief A fake `ChartWidget`: properties `yRange` and `xRange` (`[lo,hi]`), `yLabel`, `yTicks`
1591/// (`[text@value,…]`), `lines` (`[label@value;tone;style,…]`), `series` (as `formatChartSeries` gives it) and
1592/// `summary`, each set only when it changed. Numbers are written shortest-round-trip, so a log is the same on
1593/// every platform.
1594class FakeChart final : public FakeLeaf<ChartWidget> {
1595public:
1596 using FakeLeaf<ChartWidget>::FakeLeaf;
1597 void setData(ChartData const& data) override {
1598 update("yRange", std::format("[{},{}]", data.yMin, data.yMax));
1599 update("xRange", std::format("[{},{}]", data.xMin, data.xMax));
1600 update("yLabel", formatText(data.yLabel));
1601 update("yTicks", formatList(data.yTicks, [](ChartTick const& tick) {
1602 return formatChartText(tick.text) + "@" + std::format("{}", tick.value);
1603 }));
1604 update("lines", formatList(data.lines, [](ChartLine const& line) {
1605 return formatChartText(line.label) + "@" + std::format("{}", line.value) + ";" +
1606 chartToneName(line.tone) + ";" + chartStyleName(line.style);
1607 }));
1608 update("series", formatChartSeries(data.series));
1609 update("summary", formatText(data.summary));
1610 }
1611
1612private:
1613 // Logs a property only when its text differs from what is recorded, so a test sees which parts changed.
1614 void update(std::string_view name, std::string value) {
1615 auto const& props = store().at(id()).props;
1616 auto const found = props.find(name);
1617 if (found != props.end() && found->second == value) {
1618 return;
1619 }
1620 set(name, std::move(value));
1621 }
1622};

1710 }

1712 _multiple = multiple;
1713 set("multiple", formatBool(multiple));
1714 }
1715 void setOnDrop(std::function<void(std::vector<std::string>)> onDrop) override {
1716 callbacks().files = std::move(onDrop);
1717 }

1719 /// @brief Whether the zone takes a drop of @p paths: one file unless several are allowed, each with an accepted
1720 /// extension.
1721 /// @param paths The paths dropped; not empty.
1722 /// @return True when the drop is taken.
1723 [[nodiscard]] bool takes(std::vector<std::string> const& paths) const {
1724 if (paths.size() > 1 && !_multiple) {
1725 return false;
1726 }
1727 return std::ranges::all_of(paths, [this](std::string const& path) {
1728 return _accept.empty() || std::ranges::any_of(_accept, [&path](std::string const& extension) {
1729 return endsWithIgnoringCase(path, extension);
1730 });
1731 });
1732 }
1733
1734private:
1735 [[nodiscard]] static bool endsWithIgnoringCase(std::string_view text, std::string_view suffix) {
1736 if (suffix.size() > text.size()) {
1737 return false;
1738 }
1739 auto const lower = [](char character) {
1740 return static_cast<char>(std::tolower(static_cast<unsigned char>(character)));
1741 };
1742 return std::ranges::equal(text.substr(text.size() - suffix.size()), suffix, {}, lower, lower);
1743 }
1744
1745 std::vector<std::string> _accept;
1746 bool _multiple = false;
1747};

1767/// @brief A fake `TableWidget`: properties `columns`, `selectionMode`, `selection`, `sort`, `selectColumn`,
1768/// `selectAllLabel`, and `rowKey`, `tone`, `label` and `heading` on a row.
1769///
1770/// `selection` shows the rows the widget marks: the requested keys, in the order requested, that one of its current
1771/// rows has. The requested keys are kept, so a row that arrives with one of them is marked and a row that goes is
1772/// unmarked; that re-marking is the widget's own doing and is not logged.
1773class FakeTable final : public FakeContainer<TableWidget> {
1774public:
1775 /// @brief Records the new table, appended to @p parent, and logs its creation.
1776 /// @param store Where the widget records itself.
1777 /// @param kind The kind shown in the log and the dump.
1778 /// @param parent The container it is appended to, or null for a root.
1779 FakeTable(std::shared_ptr<RecordStore> store, std::string kind, ContainerWidget const* parent)
1780 : FakeContainer<TableWidget>{std::move(store), std::move(kind), parent} {
1781 this->store().at(id()).onChildDestroyed = [this](int childId) {
1782 _rowKeys.erase(childId);
1783 _headings.erase(childId);
1784 remark();
1785 };
1786 }
1787
1788 /// @brief Removes the hook that points at this table, so nothing calls it once the table is gone, even if the
1789 /// record outlives it because recording the destruction failed.
1790 ~FakeTable() override {
1791 try {
1792 store().at(id()).onChildDestroyed = nullptr;
1793 } catch (...) { // NOLINT(bugprone-empty-catch)
1794 // No record left, so no hook to remove.
1795 }
1796 }
1797
1798 FakeTable(FakeTable const&) = delete;
1799 FakeTable& operator=(FakeTable const&) = delete;
1800 FakeTable(FakeTable&&) = delete;
1801 FakeTable& operator=(FakeTable&&) = delete;
1802
1803 /// @brief Records property `columns`, each as its escaped caption, a colon and its width, then `;align=` and
1804 /// `;valign=` where the column's alignment is not the default (`Start` across, `Center` down), and
1805 /// `;sortable=true` for a sortable column, which `RecordingBackend::clickHeader` reports, and
1806 /// `;wrap=false` for a column that keeps its text cells to one line, and `;shrink=true` for a stretch
1807 /// column that may be narrower than its header.
1808 /// @param columns The columns, in order.
1809 void setColumns(std::vector<TableColumn> const& columns) override {
1810 _sortable.clear();
1811 for (TableColumn const& column : columns) {
1812 _sortable.push_back(column.sortable);
1813 }
1814 set("columns", formatList(columns, [](TableColumn const& column) {
1815 std::string text = formatItem(column.label) + ":" + formatSizing(column.width);
1816 if (column.align != Align::Start) {
1817 text += ";align=" + formatAlign(column.align);
1818 }
1819 if (column.valign != Align::Center) {
1820 text += ";valign=" + formatAlign(column.valign);
1821 }
1822 if (column.sortable) {
1823 text += ";sortable=true";
1824 }
1825 if (!column.wrap) {
1826 text += ";wrap=false";
1827 }
1828 if (column.shrink) {
1829 text += ";shrink=true";
1830 }
1831 return text;
1832 }));
1833 }
1834
1835 /// @brief Records property `showHeader`.
1836 /// @param shown Whether the header row is drawn.
1837 void setShowHeader(bool shown) override { set("showHeader", formatBool(shown)); }
1838
1839 /// @brief Records property `selectionMode`, which `RecordingBackend::selectRows` enforces.
1840 /// @param mode None, one, or any number.
1841 void setSelectionMode(SelectionMode mode) override {
1842 _mode = mode;
1843 set("selectionMode", enumName(mode));
1844 }
1845
1846 /// @brief Records property `rowKey` on @p row, and marks the row when its key is requested.
1847 /// @param row One of this table's rows.
1848 /// @param key The row's key.
1849 /// @throws std::logic_error when @p row is not this table's child.
1850 void setRowKey(Widget& row, Key const& key) override {
1851 int const rowId = store().idOf(row);
1852 if (store().at(rowId).parent != id()) {
1853 throw std::logic_error{"RecordingBackend: setRowKey of a widget that is not this table's row"};
1854 }
1855 store().set(rowId, "rowKey", formatKey(key));
1856 _rowKeys.insert_or_assign(rowId, key);
1857 remark();
1858 }
1859
1860 /// @brief Records the row's property `heading`; a heading row is never marked, selected or activated.
1861 /// @param row One of this table's rows.
1862 /// @throws std::logic_error when @p row is not this table's child.
1863 void setRowHeading(Widget& row) override {
1864 int const rowId = store().idOf(row);
1865 if (store().at(rowId).parent != id()) {
1866 throw std::logic_error{"RecordingBackend: setRowHeading of a widget that is not this table's row"};
1867 }
1868 store().set(rowId, "heading", "true");
1869 _headings.insert(rowId);
1870 remark();
1871 }
1872
1873 /// @brief Whether the current row with @p key is a heading.
1874 /// @param key The key.
1875 /// @return False when no current row has it, or the row is a data row.
1876 [[nodiscard]] bool headingKey(Key const& key) const {
1877 std::optional<int> const row = rowOf(key);
1878 return row.has_value() && _headings.contains(*row);
1879 }
1880
1881 /// @brief Records the row's property `tone` (`none` for no tone).
1882 /// @param row One of this table's rows.
1883 /// @param tone The tone, or none.
1884 /// @throws std::logic_error when @p row is not this table's child.
1885 void setRowTone(Widget& row, std::optional<Tone> tone) override {
1886 int const rowId = store().idOf(row);
1887 if (store().at(rowId).parent != id()) {
1888 throw std::logic_error{"RecordingBackend: setRowTone of a widget that is not this table's row"};
1889 }
1890 store().set(rowId, "tone", tone ? enumName(*tone) : std::string{"none"});
1891 }
1892
1893 /// @brief Records property `selectColumn`.
1894 /// @param shown Whether the select column is drawn.
1895 void setSelectColumn(bool shown) override { set("selectColumn", formatBool(shown)); }
1896
1897 /// @brief Records property `selectAllLabel`.
1898 /// @param label The header box's name.
1899 void setSelectAllLabel(std::string_view label) override { set("selectAllLabel", formatText(label)); }

1901 /// @brief Records the row's property `label`.
1902 /// @param row One of this table's rows.
1903 /// @param label The row's name.
1904 /// @throws std::logic_error when @p row is not this table's child.

1938 /// @brief Whether the column at @p column is sortable, as `setColumns` gave it.

1941 [[nodiscard]] bool sortable(std::size_t column) const { return column < _sortable.size() && _sortable.at(column); }

1943 /// @brief Records property `realizedWindow` as `<first>+<count>/<total>`.
1944 /// @param first The view index of the first realized row.

1951 /// @brief Stores the handler `RecordingBackend::scrollTable` calls.

1954 _onVisibleRangeChanged = std::move(onVisibleRangeChanged);

1957 /// @brief Simulates the backend reporting a scroll: calls the handler `setOnVisibleRangeChanged` stored, as a
1958 /// real backend's own scroll callback would. Does nothing if nothing is subscribed (a table below its
1959 /// virtualization threshold never calls `setOnVisibleRangeChanged`, so this is a silent no-op for it,
1960 /// matching a real backend that never virtualizes).
1961 /// @param first The view index of the first row now wanted.
1962 /// @param count How many rows from `first` are wanted.
1963 void scrollTo(std::size_t first, std::size_t count) {
1964 if (_onVisibleRangeChanged) {
1965 _onVisibleRangeChanged(first, count);
1966 }

1969 /// @brief The selection mode last set.
1970 /// @return The mode; `None` until `setSelectionMode` runs.
1971 [[nodiscard]] SelectionMode mode() const noexcept { return _mode; }

1973 /// @brief The current row with @p key.
1974 /// @param key The key.
1975 /// @return The row's id, or `nullopt` when no current row has @p key.
1976 [[nodiscard]] std::optional<int> rowOf(Key const& key) const {
1977 for (int const child : store().at(id()).children) {
1978 if (auto const found = _rowKeys.find(child); found != _rowKeys.end() && found->second == key) {
1979 return child;
1980 }
1981 }
1982 return std::nullopt;
1983 }

1985 /// @brief Marks the rows the user selected, as the requested keys; nothing is logged. The last key becomes the
1986 /// anchor of a later Shift-click.
1987 /// @param keys Keys of current rows.
1988 void selectByUser(std::vector<Key> const& keys) {
1989 if (!keys.empty()) {
1990 _anchor = keys.back();
1991 }
1992 select(keys);
1993 }
1994
1995 /// @brief Marks the rows a user's click or key selected, as the requested keys, leaving the anchor where the
1996 /// input left it; nothing is logged.
1997 /// @param keys Keys of current rows.
1998 void select(std::vector<Key> const& keys) {
1999 _requested = keys;
2000 remark();
2001 }
2002
2003 /// @brief What a click on the row with @p key selects, as every backend's selection model has it, and makes
2004 /// the clicked row the anchor unless the click was a range.
2005 /// @param key A current row's key.
2006 /// @param click How the click was modified.
2007 /// @return The keys then selected, in row order for a range, and the kind of change.
2008 [[nodiscard]] std::pair<std::vector<Key>, SelectionChange> clicked(Key const& key, RowClick click) {
2009 if (_mode != SelectionMode::Multiple || click == RowClick::Only) {
2010 _anchor = key;
2011 return {{key}, SelectionChange::Replace};
2012 }
2013 if (click == RowClick::Toggle) {
2014 _anchor = key;
2015 std::vector<Key> next = markedKeys();
2016 if (auto const found = std::ranges::find(next, key); found != next.end()) {
2017 next.erase(found);
2018 } else {
2019 next.push_back(key);
2020 }
2021 return {next, SelectionChange::Extend};
2022 }
2023 std::vector<Key> const rows = rowKeys();
2024 Key const from = _anchor.has_value() && rowOf(*_anchor).has_value() ? *_anchor : key;
2025 auto const first = std::ranges::find(rows, from);
2026 auto const last = std::ranges::find(rows, key);
2027 auto const [low, high] = std::minmax(first, last);
2028 return {std::vector<Key>{low, std::next(high)}, SelectionChange::Replace};
2029 }
2030
2031 /// @brief What Ctrl+A selects in a `Multiple` table: every row, or none when every row is selected already.
2032 /// @return The keys, in row order.
2033 [[nodiscard]] std::vector<Key> allOrNone() const {
2034 std::vector<Key> const rows = rowKeys();
2035 std::vector<Key> const marked = markedKeys();
2036 bool const every =
2037 std::ranges::all_of(rows, [&marked](Key const& key) { return std::ranges::contains(marked, key); });
2038 return every ? std::vector<Key>{} : rows;
2039 }
2040
2041 /// @brief The keys of the current data rows, in row order: a heading row is not one.
2042 /// @return The keys.
2043 [[nodiscard]] std::vector<Key> rowKeys() const {
2044 std::vector<Key> keys;
2045 for (int const child : store().at(id()).children) {
2046 if (auto const found = _rowKeys.find(child); found != _rowKeys.end() && !_headings.contains(child)) {
2047 keys.push_back(found->second);
2048 }
2049 }
2050 return keys;
2051 }
2052
2053 /// @brief The keys of the rows the table marks: the requested keys, in the order requested, that a current row
2054 /// has.
2055 /// @return The keys.
2056 [[nodiscard]] std::vector<Key> markedKeys() const {
2057 std::vector<Key> keys;
2058 for (Key const& key : _requested.value_or(std::vector<Key>{})) {
2059 if (rowOf(key).has_value() && !headingKey(key)) {
2060 keys.push_back(key);
2061 }
2062 }
2063 return keys;
2064 }
2065
2066private:
2067 [[nodiscard]] std::string marked() const {
2068 return formatList(markedKeys(), [](Key const& key) { return formatKey(key); });
2069 }
2070
2071 void remark() {
2072 if (_requested.has_value()) {
2073 store().setByUser(id(), "selection", marked());
2074 }
2075 }
2076
2077 SelectionMode _mode = SelectionMode::None;
2078 std::vector<bool> _sortable; // per column, as setColumns gave them
2079 std::set<int> _headings; // the heading rows' ids
2080 std::map<int, Key> _rowKeys; // row id -> key, as setRowKey told it
2081 // Engaged once `setSelection` ran or the user selected.
2082 std::optional<std::vector<Key>> _requested;
2083 // The row a Shift-click's range starts from: the last row clicked without Shift.
2084 std::optional<Key> _anchor;
2085 std::function<void(std::size_t, std::size_t)> _onVisibleRangeChanged;
2086};

2090/// @brief A headless `IViewBackend`: fake widgets that record every operation, a golden dump of the live tree, and
2091/// helpers that act as the user would.
2092///
2093/// Widget ids are creation numbers from 1. A widget ignores every interaction helper, as a real one would, while it
2094/// is hidden or disabled, or while a container around it is hidden, disabled or collapsed. A dialog, and everything
2095/// inside it, ignores them until it is opened. A helper used on a kind of widget it does not apply to throws
2096/// `std::logic_error`: that is a mistake in the test, not something a user can do. A helper copies the handler before
2097/// calling it, so a handler may destroy its own widget.
2098///
2099/// Free text in a property value is escaped as `detail::formatText` and `detail::formatItem` describe, so every
2100/// value stays on its line and reads as one field, or one list element.
2101class RecordingBackend final : public IViewBackend {
2102public:

2230 /// @brief The width class it reports: `expanded`, the class of a surface with no width, until `setWidthClass`.
2231 /// @return The class.
2232 [[nodiscard]] std::string widthClass() const override { return _widthClass; }
2233
2234 /// @brief Registers the listener `setWidthClass` tells of a change; it is not called at once.
2235 /// @param onWidthClass The listener; empty clears it.

2288 /// @brief The first live widget, by id, of a kind whose property has a value.
2289 /// @param kind The kind, as the dump shows it.
2290 /// @param name The property.
2291 /// @param value Its formatted value.
2292 /// @return The widget's id, or `nullopt`.
2293 // The contract's lookup: kind, property name and value, all text.
2294 // NOLINTNEXTLINE(bugprone-easily-swappable-parameters)
2295 [[nodiscard]] std::optional<int> find(std::string_view kind, std::string_view name, std::string_view value) const {
2296 for (auto const& [widgetId, record] : _store->records()) {
2297 if (record.kind != kind) {
2298 continue;
2299 }
2300 if (auto const found = record.props.find(name); found != record.props.end() && found->second == value) {
2301 return widgetId;
2302 }
2303 }
2304 return std::nullopt;
2305 }

2372
2373 /// @brief Presses a keyboard chord with focus on a widget, in the key order every backend follows.
2374 ///
2375 /// First a chord @p widgetId declares itself through `setKeys`. Then the built-in keys of its kind: a `Button`'s
2376 /// `Enter` or `Space` clicks it; a single-line or password `TextInput`'s `Enter` commits, then submits and stops
2377 /// when the field has a submit handler, and goes on after the commit when it has none; a `Checkbox`'s `Space`
2378 /// toggles it; a segmented `Select`'s `Left` and `Right` choose the previous or the next option, stopping at the
2379 /// ends; a `Table`'s `Enter` activates its first marked row, and stops whether or not one is marked; a
2380 /// `Multiple` table's `Ctrl+A` selects every row, or clears them when every row is selected, as `Extend`. Then
2381 /// the chords of its ancestors, innermost first. A handler that destroys the focused widget stops the key there.
2382 /// Like every helper it acts only when a user could reach @p widgetId.
2383 /// @param widgetId The widget focus is on.
2384 /// @param chord The chord, as declared, such as `"Ctrl+S"`, `"Enter"` or `"Space"`.
2385 /// @return True when any step took the chord.
2386 bool press(int widgetId, std::string const& chord) {
2387 detail::Record const& focused = _store->at(widgetId);
2388 if (!reachable(focused)) {
2389 return false;
2390 }
2391 int const parent = focused.parent;
2392 if (std::ranges::find(focused.chords, chord) != focused.chords.end()) {
2393 invoke(focused.callbacks.chord, chord);
2394 return true;
2395 }
2396 if (ownKey(widgetId, chord) || !exists(widgetId)) {
2397 return true;
2398 }
2399 for (int candidate = parent; candidate != 0;) {
2400 detail::Record const& record = _store->at(candidate);
2401 if (std::ranges::find(record.chords, chord) != record.chords.end()) {
2402 invoke(record.callbacks.chord, chord);
2403 return true;
2404 }
2405 candidate = record.parent;
2406 }
2407 return false;
2408 }

2419 /// @brief Activates a button, or the action button of a banner or an empty state. A widget inside a list entry's
2420 /// content activates the entry: its content takes no input of its own.
2421 /// @param widgetId The button, banner or empty state, or a widget inside an entry's content.
2422 /// @throws std::logic_error when the widget is none of those, or is a banner or empty state that shows no action
2423 /// button.
2424 void click(int widgetId) {
2425 if (std::string const kind = kindOf(widgetId); kind != "Button" && kind != "Banner" && kind != "EmptyState") {
2426 for (int outer = _store->at(widgetId).parent; outer != 0; outer = _store->at(outer).parent) {
2427 if (_store->at(outer).kind == "Button") {
2428 widgetId = outer;
2429 break;
2430 }
2431 }
2432 }
2433 detail::Record const& record = expectKind(widgetId, "click", {"Button", "Banner", "EmptyState"});
2434 if (record.kind != "Button" && prop(widgetId, "actionLabel").empty()) {
2435 throw std::logic_error{"RecordingBackend: click of " + record.kind + "#" + std::to_string(widgetId) +
2436 ", which shows no action button"};

2438 if (reachable(record)) {
2439 invoke(record.kind == "Button" ? record.callbacks.click : record.callbacks.action);
2440 }
2441 }

2550 /// @brief Chooses an entry of a menu by its path, as a user opening each submenu on the way would.

2553 /// runs), or an entry that is disabled or inside a disabled entry.
2554 /// @param widgetId The menu.
2555 /// @param path The entry's index at each level, from the top.
2556 /// @throws std::logic_error when the widget is not a menu.
2557 void chooseMenuEntry(int widgetId, std::vector<std::size_t> const& path) {
2558 detail::Record const* const record = actionable(widgetId, "chooseMenuEntry", {"Menu"});
2559 if (record == nullptr) {
2560 return;
2561 }
2562 std::vector<MenuEntry> const* level = &record->menu;
2563 MenuEntry const* entry = nullptr;
2564 for (std::size_t const index : path) {
2565 if (level == nullptr || index >= level->size() || !level->at(index).enabled ||
2566 level->at(index).separator) {
2567 return;
2568 }
2569 entry = &level->at(index);
2570 level = &entry->items;
2571 }
2572 if (entry != nullptr && entry->items.empty()) {
2573 invoke(record->callbacks.path, path);
2574 }
2575 }

2683 /// @brief Selects rows of a table by key: the table marks them, then `onSelectionChange` gets the keys.
2684 /// @param widgetId The table.
2685 /// @param keys The keys of every row the user now selects, in the order selected.
2686 /// @throws std::logic_error when the widget is not a table, or the selection is not one a user could make: a key
2687 /// that names no current data row (a heading is not one), a row twice, any row in a `None` table, or more
2688 /// than one in a `Single` one.
2689 void selectRows(int widgetId, std::vector<Key> keys) {
2690 detail::Record const& record = expectKind(widgetId, "selectRows", {"Table"});
2691 auto* const table = dynamic_cast<detail::FakeTable*>(record.widget);
2692 std::string const where = " of Table#" + std::to_string(widgetId);
2693 if (table == nullptr || table->mode() == SelectionMode::None) {
2694 throw std::logic_error{"RecordingBackend: selectRows" + where + ", which selects nothing"};
2695 }
2696 if (table->mode() == SelectionMode::Single && keys.size() > 1) {
2697 throw std::logic_error{"RecordingBackend: selectRows of several rows" + where + ", which selects one"};
2698 }
2699 std::unordered_set<Key> seen;
2700 for (Key const& key : keys) {
2701 if (!table->rowOf(key).has_value() || table->headingKey(key) || !seen.insert(key).second) {
2702 throw std::logic_error{"RecordingBackend: selectRows of " + detail::formatKey(key) + where +
2703 ", which has no such row or selects it twice"};
2704 }
2705 }
2706 if (reachable(record)) {
2707 table->selectByUser(keys);
2708 invoke(record.callbacks.selection, std::move(keys), SelectionChange::Replace);
2709 }
2710 }
2711
2712 /// @brief Clicks a row of a table as the user would with the click's modifiers: the table marks what the click
2713 /// selects (`TableWidget`'s selection model), then `onSelectionChange` gets the keys and the kind of
2714 /// change, `Replace` for a plain click or a range and `Extend` for a toggle. A click on a heading row
2715 /// does nothing, as a user's does.
2716 /// @param widgetId The table.
2717 /// @param key The row's key.
2718 /// @param click How the click is modified.
2719 /// @throws std::logic_error when the widget is not a table, it selects nothing, or no current row has @p key.
2720 void clickRow(int widgetId, Key const& key, RowClick click) {
2721 detail::Record const& record = expectKind(widgetId, "clickRow", {"Table"});
2722 auto* const table = dynamic_cast<detail::FakeTable*>(record.widget);
2723 std::string const where = " of Table#" + std::to_string(widgetId);
2724 if (table == nullptr || table->mode() == SelectionMode::None) {
2725 throw std::logic_error{"RecordingBackend: clickRow" + where + ", which selects nothing"};
2726 }
2727 std::optional<int> const rowId = table->rowOf(key);
2728 if (!rowId.has_value()) {
2729 throw std::logic_error{"RecordingBackend: clickRow of " + detail::formatKey(key) + where +
2730 ", which has no such row"};
2731 }
2732 // A click on a heading row selects nothing, as a user's does.
2733 if (!reachable(record) || !reachable(_store->at(*rowId)) || table->headingKey(key)) {
2734 return;
2735 }
2736 auto [keys, change] = table->clicked(key, click);
2737 table->select(keys);
2738 invoke(record.callbacks.selection, std::move(keys), change);
2739 }

2741 /// @brief Clicks a column's header as the user would: a sortable column's reaches `onSort` with its index; any
2742 /// other header does nothing, since a user can click it.

2744 /// @param column The column's index among the columns `setColumns` gave.
2745 /// @throws std::logic_error when the widget is not a table.
2746 // NOLINTNEXTLINE(bugprone-easily-swappable-parameters)
2747 void clickHeader(int widgetId, std::size_t column) {
2748 detail::Record const& record = expectKind(widgetId, "clickHeader", {"Table"});
2749 auto const* const table = dynamic_cast<detail::FakeTable const*>(record.widget);
2750 if (table != nullptr && table->sortable(column) && reachable(record)) {
2751 invoke(record.callbacks.sort, column);

2755 /// @brief Activates a row of a table (Enter or a double click).
2756 /// @param widgetId The table.

2758 /// @throws std::logic_error when the widget is not a table, or none of its current data rows has @p key.
2759 void activateRow(int widgetId, Key key) {
2760 detail::Record const& record = expectKind(widgetId, "activateRow", {"Table"});
2761 auto const* const table = dynamic_cast<detail::FakeTable const*>(record.widget);
2762 std::optional<int> const rowId = table == nullptr ? std::nullopt : table->rowOf(key);
2763 if (!rowId.has_value() || table->headingKey(key)) {
2764 throw std::logic_error{"RecordingBackend: activateRow of " + detail::formatKey(key) + ", which Table#" +
2765 std::to_string(widgetId) + " has no data row for"};
2766 }
2767 if (reachable(_store->at(*rowId))) {
2768 invoke(record.callbacks.activate, std::move(key));
2769 }

2772 /// @brief Simulates the backend reporting a scroll on a virtualized table, as a real Qt Quick table's own
2773 /// scroll handling would: calls the handler `IViewBackend::TableWidget::setOnVisibleRangeChanged`
2774 /// subscribed, so the mount realizes/releases rows to match. A table whose row count is below its
2775 /// `Virtualization::threshold` never subscribes one, so this call does nothing for it, matching a real
2776 /// backend that never virtualizes a small table.
2777 /// @param widgetId The table.
2778 /// @param first The view index of the first row now wanted.
2779 /// @param count How many rows from `first` are wanted.
2780 /// @throws std::logic_error when the widget is not a table.
2781 void scrollTable(int widgetId, std::size_t first, std::size_t count) {

2783 auto* const table = dynamic_cast<detail::FakeTable*>(record.widget);
2784 if (table == nullptr) {
2785 throw std::logic_error{"RecordingBackend: scrollTable of Table#" + std::to_string(widgetId) +
2786 ", which is not a table"};

2788 table->scrollTo(first, count);

2791 /// @brief Enters a date-time, or clears the field with `nullopt`.

2795 void setDateTime(int widgetId, std::optional<morph::time::Timestamp> value) {
2796 if (detail::Record const* const record = editable(widgetId, "setDateTime", {"DateTimeInput"});
2797 record != nullptr) {
2798 _store->setByUser(widgetId, "value", detail::formatTimestamp(value));

2803 /// @brief Moves a slider to @p value, a finished move: `onChange` gets it, then `onCommit`.
2804 /// @param widgetId The slider.
2805 /// @param value The value moved to.
2806 /// @throws std::logic_error when the widget is not a slider.
2807 void slide(int widgetId, std::int64_t value) {
2808 if (detail::Record const* const record = editable(widgetId, "slide", {"Slider"}); record != nullptr) {
2809 _store->setByUser(widgetId, "value", std::to_string(value));
2810 // The change handler may destroy the slider, so the commit handler is copied before either runs.
2811 auto const commit = record->callbacks.slideCommit;
2812 invoke(record->callbacks.slide, value);
2813 invoke(commit, value);
2814 }
2815 }

2817 /// @brief Moves a slider to @p value while the move is still in progress: `onChange` gets it, and `onCommit` does
2818 /// not run until the move finishes. Named apart from `drag`, which drags one widget onto another.
2819 /// @param widgetId The slider.
2820 /// @param value The value moved to.
2821 /// @throws std::logic_error when the widget is not a slider.
2822 void dragSlider(int widgetId, std::int64_t value) {
2823 if (detail::Record const* const record = editable(widgetId, "dragSlider", {"Slider"}); record != nullptr) {
2824 _store->setByUser(widgetId, "value", std::to_string(value));
2825 invoke(record->callbacks.slide, value);

2832 /// @throws std::logic_error when the widget is not a file picker.
2833 void pick(int widgetId, std::string path) {
2834 if (detail::Record const* const record = editable(widgetId, "pick", {"FilePicker"}); record != nullptr) {
2835 _store->setByUser(widgetId, "path", detail::formatText(path));
2836 invoke(record->callbacks.picked, std::move(path));

2840 /// @brief Drags one widget onto another. Any kind of widget can be a source or a target.
2841 ///
2842 /// An empty `accepts` refuses every key: the mount always passes a predicate, so a drop that lands without
2843 /// one shows the mount's accept-everything default at work rather than this backend's leniency.
2844 /// @param sourceId The dragged widget; it must have a drag key.
2845 /// @param targetId The widget dropped on; it must be a drop target whose `accepts` holds for the key.
2846 /// @return True when the drop was accepted and `onDrop` ran.
2847 /// @throws std::logic_error when @p sourceId and @p targetId are the same widget.
2848 bool drag(int sourceId, int targetId) {
2849 if (sourceId == targetId) {
2850 throw std::logic_error{"RecordingBackend: drag of a widget onto itself"};
2851 }
2852 detail::Record const& source = _store->at(sourceId);
2853 detail::Record const& target = _store->at(targetId);
2854 if (!reachable(source) || !reachable(target)) {
2855 return false;
2856 }
2857 std::optional<Key> const key = source.dragKey;
2858 auto const accepts = target.callbacks.accepts;
2859 auto const drop = target.callbacks.drop;
2860 if (!key.has_value() || !drop || !accepts || !accepts(*key)) {
2861 return false;
2862 }
2863 drop(*key);
2864 return true;
2865 }

2867private:
2868 // The fake behind a text field's record.
2869 static detail::FakeTextInput& textInput(detail::Record const& record) {
2870 return dynamic_cast<detail::FakeTextInput&>(*record.widget);
2871 }
2872
2873 // The built-in keys of the focused widget's kind, `press`'s second step: whether the key stops here. A text input
2874 // without a submit handler commits on Enter and lets the key go on.
2875 // Left or Right on a segmented select: chooses the neighbour, if any, as a user's choice.
2876 void stepSegmented(int widgetId, bool forward) {
2877 auto const* const select = dynamic_cast<detail::FakeSelect const*>(_store->at(widgetId).widget);
2878 std::optional<Key> next = select == nullptr ? std::nullopt : select->neighbour(forward ? 1 : -1);
2879 if (next.has_value()) {
2880 choose(widgetId, std::move(*next));
2881 }
2882 }
2883
2884 bool ownKey(int widgetId, std::string const& chord) {
2885 detail::Record const& record = _store->at(widgetId);
2886 bool const enter = chord == "Enter";
2887 if (record.kind == "Button" && (enter || chord == "Space")) {
2888 invoke(record.callbacks.click);
2889 return true;
2890 }
2891 if (record.kind == "Checkbox" && chord == "Space") {
2892 toggle(widgetId);
2893 return true;
2894 }
2895 if (record.kind == "Select" && prop(widgetId, "style") == "Segmented" &&
2896 (chord == "Left" || chord == "Right")) {
2897 stepSegmented(widgetId, chord == "Right");
2898 return true;
2899 }
2900 if (record.kind == "TextInput" && enter && prop(widgetId, "mode") != "Multiline") {
2901 if (record.callbacks.submit) {
2902 submit(widgetId, textInput(record).text());
2903 return true;
2904 }
2905 commit(widgetId);
2906 return false;
2907 }
2908 if (record.kind == "Table" && chord == "Ctrl+A") {
2909 auto* const table = dynamic_cast<detail::FakeTable*>(record.widget);
2910 if (table == nullptr || table->mode() != SelectionMode::Multiple) {
2911 return false;
2912 }
2913 std::vector<Key> keys = table->allOrNone();
2914 table->select(keys);
2915 invoke(record.callbacks.selection, std::move(keys), SelectionChange::Extend);
2916 return true;
2917 }
2918 if (record.kind == "Table" && enter) {
2919 auto const* const table = dynamic_cast<detail::FakeTable const*>(record.widget);
2920 std::vector<Key> const marked = table == nullptr ? std::vector<Key>{} : table->markedKeys();
2921 if (!marked.empty()) {
2922 activateRow(widgetId, marked.front());
2923 }
2924 return true;
2925 }
2926 return false;
2927 }
2928
2929 // A helper applies to some kinds only; using it on another kind is a mistake in the test, not a user action.
2930 detail::Record& expectKind(int widgetId, std::string_view helper, std::initializer_list<std::string_view> kinds) {
2931 detail::Record& record = _store->at(widgetId);
2932 if (std::ranges::find(kinds, std::string_view{record.kind}) == kinds.end()) {
2933 throw std::logic_error{"RecordingBackend: " + std::string{helper} + " does not apply to " + record.kind +
2934 "#" + std::to_string(widgetId)};
2935 }
2936 return record;
2937 }
2938
2939 // The widget's record when a user could reach it now, else null.
2940 [[nodiscard]] detail::Record* actionable(int widgetId, std::string_view helper,
2941 std::initializer_list<std::string_view> kinds) {
2942 detail::Record& record = expectKind(widgetId, helper, kinds);
2943 return reachable(record) ? &record : nullptr;
2944 }
2945
2946 // The widget's record when a user could reach it now and change its value, else null.
2947 [[nodiscard]] detail::Record* editable(int widgetId, std::string_view helper,
2948 std::initializer_list<std::string_view> kinds) {
2949 detail::Record* const record = actionable(widgetId, helper, kinds);
2950 return record != nullptr && !flagIs(*record, "readonly", true) ? record : nullptr;
2951 }
2952
2953 // A user reaches a widget that is shown and enabled, inside containers that are all shown, enabled and not
2954 // collapsed. A collapsed panel's own collapse control stays reachable, so only an outer panel's state counts. A
2955 // dialog shows nothing, itself included, until it is opened.
2956 [[nodiscard]] bool reachable(detail::Record const& record) const {
2957 if (flagIs(record, "visible", false) || flagIs(record, "enabled", false) || isClosedDialog(record)) {
2958 return false;
2959 }
2960 for (int innerId = record.id, outerId = record.parent; outerId != 0;) {
2961 detail::Record const& outer = _store->at(outerId);
2962 if (flagIs(outer, "visible", false) || flagIs(outer, "enabled", false) ||
2963 flagIs(outer, "collapsed", true) || isClosedDialog(outer) || closedAround(outer, innerId)) {
2964 return false;
2965 }
2966 innerId = outerId;
2967 outerId = outer.parent;
2968 }
2969 return true;
2970 }
2971
2972 // A dialog or drawer shows nothing until it is opened.
2973 [[nodiscard]] static bool isClosedDialog(detail::Record const& record) {
2974 return (record.kind == "Dialog" || record.kind == "Drawer") && !flagIs(record, "open", true);
2975 }
2976
2977 // A closed collapsible section hides its content, the child on the way in, unless that child is its header.
2978 [[nodiscard]] static bool closedAround(detail::Record const& outer, int childId) {
2979 if (outer.kind != "Collapsible" || !flagIs(outer, "open", false)) {
2980 return false;
2981 }
2982 auto const header = outer.props.find("header");
2983 return header == outer.props.end() || header->second != std::to_string(childId);
2984 }
2985
2986 [[nodiscard]] static bool flagIs(detail::Record const& record, std::string_view name, bool value) {
2987 auto const found = record.props.find(name);
2988 return found != record.props.end() && found->second == detail::formatBool(value);
2989 }
2990
2991 // The copy keeps the handler alive while it runs, even when it destroys the widget it was stored on.
2992 template <typename... Args, typename... Values>
2993 static void invoke(std::function<void(Args...)> const& handler, Values&&... values) {
2994 auto const copy = handler;
2995 if (copy) {
2996 copy(std::forward<Values>(values)...);
2997 }
2998 }
2999
3000 std::shared_ptr<detail::RecordStore> _store = std::make_shared<detail::RecordStore>();
3001 std::unordered_set<std::string> _components;
3002 std::string _widthClass = "expanded";
3003 std::function<void(std::string const&)> _onWidthClass;
3004};
